h1: Strategy for teams who do the work themselves
metaTitle: SEO Consulting Services — 8 Hours a Month, ₹40,000
metaDescription: SEO consulting services for teams that execute in-house. Eight hours a month of strategy, review and priority calls at ₹40,000, plus honest advice to stop.
answer: SEO consulting is advice without execution. You already have a writer and a developer; you need someone to decide what they work on next and to check whether it worked. Eight hours a month, ₹40,000 ex-GST, month to month. We don't write, build or do outreach on this plan.
takeaways: This is for teams **with hands already**. One writer and one developer with capacity is the minimum. Without them, consulting produces a roadmap that nobody executes.
Eight hours a month, ₹40,000 ex-GST, month to month. Roughly two calls plus review time between them.
**No outcome guarantee applies**, because we don't control execution. Our normal 90-day baseline guarantee is for retainers where we do the work.
We end the engagement when your team stops needing the calls. That's the goal, not a failure state.

body: There's a specific company shape where consulting beats a retainer, and it's narrower than the people selling consulting will admit.

You have a marketer who can write, or a writer who can be briefed. You have a developer, in-house or on contract, with real capacity in the sprint. Someone owns the CMS and can publish without raising a ticket. What you don't have is anyone who knows which of the forty possible things to do next, or whether last month's work actually did anything.
That's a direction problem, not a capacity problem, and it's badly served by a full retainer. You'd be paying us ₹75,000 a month to duplicate people you already employ.
bullets: **Good fit:** a Series A SaaS with a content marketer and an engineering team, a D2C brand with an in-house content pod, an agency wanting a second opinion on their own SEO, a founder who is genuinely doing the work and needs a sounding board with skin in it.

**Bad fit:** nobody to write, no developer access, a team already at capacity on other work, or an expectation that advice alone moves rankings. In those cases we say so on the first call and point you at the [full retainer](/pricing) or nothing at all.

callout.title: The failure mode
callout.body: Consulting fails the same way every time. Month one produces a good roadmap. Month two, nothing has shipped because the writer got pulled onto a launch. Month three we review the same roadmap. By month four you're paying ₹40,000 a month for a meeting. We call this out the first time it happens, not the third.

sections.h2: What the eight hours actually cover
body: Advisory time gets spent on decisions, review and unblocking. It does not get spent on production, and the distinction is the whole point of the plan.

In practice a month looks like two calls of 60 to 90 minutes with asynchronous review work between them. You get a shared document that stays current and a Slack or WhatsApp channel for the questions that don't need a call.
numbered: **The roadmap, and the ordering of it.** What gets built next quarter and, more usefully, what gets dropped. Most in-house SEO plans fail on sequencing rather than on ideas.

**Keyword and topic decisions.** Which clusters are worth your team's time given your authority today, and which are a two-year fight you'll lose. We'll tell you when a keyword is out of reach and why.
**Content and technical review.** We read what your team shipped and mark it up. Briefs before writing, drafts after, templates before your developer builds them.

**Diagnosis when something breaks.** Rankings drop, indexing stalls, a release goes wrong. This is where the retainer of hours earns its keep — you get an experienced read within a day instead of a fortnight of guessing.
**Hiring and tooling input.** The job description, the interview questions, the paid test task, and a straight answer on whether you need Ahrefs, Semrush or neither at your stage.
**Reviewing other vendors.** Plenty of clients use these hours to audit the agency they already pay. It's an uncomfortable service to offer and a genuinely useful one.

callout.title: When you need execution instead
callout.body: Some of this can be bought separately as a fixed project — a [migration](/services/site-migration-seo), an audit, a schema build — without moving to a full retainer. We'll say which applies rather than pushing you up a tier.

sections.h2: ₹40,000 a month, and what happens to unused hours
body: One number, one scope, no annual commitment.
bullets: **₹40,000 a month, ex-GST, for eight hours.** Billed monthly in advance, month to month from the start — no first-quarter minimum, because advisory doesn't need one.
**Unused hours don't roll over.** They also don't get padded to fill the invoice. A quiet month is a quiet month, and if you have three in a row we'll suggest pausing.
**Overrun is billed at the same effective rate**, agreed in advance, never applied as a surprise. Most months land close to eight.
**Thirty days' notice, no exit fee.** Every document, brief and roadmap we produce is yours to keep, including if you take it to another agency the following week.

**Compare that with the [SEO retainer](/pricing) at ₹75,000/mo**, where we do the work rather than direct it. The gap between the two prices is roughly what execution costs — which is a useful thing to know when you're deciding whether to hire in-house.

sections.h2: Consulting or the full retainer — how to choose, and when to switch
body: The honest test is capacity, not budget. If the roadmap would ship either way, consulting is cheaper. If it wouldn't, consulting is the more expensive option because it produces nothing.

sections.h2: Why there's no guarantee on this plan
body: Everywhere else on this site we make the same commitment: freeze your trailing-90-day count of qualified leads from organic search on day one, and if we haven't beaten it in 90 days we keep working free until we do. We never promise a specific ranking position — nobody controls Google's index.

That guarantee is off the table for consulting, and it should be. It works because we control the work. On an advisory plan we control the advice and nothing else. If your writer ships two articles instead of eight because a funding round ate the quarter, the advice was still right and the outcome still didn't arrive. Charging us for that would be unfair; pretending otherwise to win the deal would be worse.

What we do commit to is narrower and checkable. You get an opinion with reasoning attached, not a hedge. When we're unsure, we say the range and why. And when the honest answer is that SEO isn't your constraint this quarter, you'll hear that on a call you paid for — which is arguably the highest-value ₹40,000 we ever bill.

sections.h2: How the engagement is supposed to end
body: Most advisory retainers are designed to be permanent. A monthly call, a familiar face, an invoice that renews itself quietly for three years. It's a comfortable business and it's not the one we're running.

There's a point on most engagements — often somewhere between month six and month twelve — where the calls get shorter and you're mostly telling us what you already decided. That's the signal. We'll raise it before you do, and we'll suggest dropping to a quarterly check-in or stopping outright.

The exceptions are real and we're not pretending otherwise. Sites in genuinely competitive markets, teams with regular turnover, and businesses replatforming or expanding into new markets keep needing the direction. But the default assumption is that we're temporary, and if that ends up costing us a client who'd have paid for another eighteen months, that's the design working — the same reason we [only take three clients a month](/journal/why-we-only-take-three-clients-a-month).

faqs.q: How much does an SEO consultant cost in India?
faqs.a: Independent consultants in India typically charge ₹2,000–₹15,000 an hour, or ₹25,000–₹1,50,000 a month on retainer depending on seniority. Ours is ₹40,000 a month ex-GST for eight hours, month to month, advisory only — no writing, building or outreach included.

faqs.q: What's the difference between SEO consulting and an SEO retainer?
faqs.a: Consulting is direction; a retainer is direction plus execution. On consulting we decide what to do and review what your team shipped. On a retainer we do the writing, the technical fixes and the outreach ourselves. The price gap between them is roughly what execution costs.

faqs.q: Can eight hours a month really be enough?
faqs.a: For direction, usually yes — decisions don't take that long once someone knows your site. For production, obviously not. If your bottleneck is that nobody has time to write or build, eight hours of advice makes the bottleneck more visible, not smaller.

faqs.q: Do you offer a guarantee on consulting?
faqs.a: No, deliberately. Our 90-day baseline guarantee applies where we control the work. On advisory we control the advice and not the execution, so guaranteeing an outcome would be selling certainty we don't have. It's month to month with 30 days' notice instead.

faqs.q: Can I use consulting to review my current SEO agency?
faqs.a: Yes, and a fair number of clients do. We'll read the reports, check what actually shipped against what was promised, and give you a straight read on whether the work is worth the fee. We won't pitch to replace them inside that engagement.
